label: prf:topological-mass-transient-localisation
title: Proof that transient terms localise to exceptional divisors
html:
Proof. Proof that transient terms localise to exceptional divisors

Proof. The transient component \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) is annihilated by \hat{\tau}_n: it lies in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker\hat{\tau}_n (descent eigenspaces). By the structure of the defining boundary (brane boundary), the support of a transient section is contained in a neighbourhood of the boundary \partial \mathcal{S}_n, which has codimension \geq 2 in \mathcal{S}_n (item (1)) and whose fibre at each blow-up centre p_i is the exceptional divisor E_i \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) (item (2)).

On the surface \Sigma, the transient integrand is therefore supported on the discs D_i centred at the blow-up points. Since the D_i are disjoint (each blow-up introduces a new connected component of \partial \mathcal{S}_n), the multiplicative integral splits as a product:

  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)\bigr)
  = 
  \prod_{i=1}^{N}
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{D_i}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr).

Since the D_i are geometrically disjoint and the group elements commute up to the central band \mathcal{O}_M^{\times} of the gerbe (the transient modes are localised at distinct points, and the central extension ensures that the group-valued integrals commute modulo the band), the norm of the product equals the sum of the norms:

  \bigl\lVert
  \prod_{i=1}^{N}
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{D_i}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert
  = 
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{E_i}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert,

where we replace D_i by E_i since the integrand is supported on the exceptional fibre E_i \subset D_i. \square
